headline: Motilal Oswal names top capital goods stock picks
hook: Brokerage identifies top capital goods sector picks

modes.bear: Brokerage picks are subjective and may not outperform the broader market or sector indices.
modes.bull: Brokerage backing suggests strong fundamentals and growth prospects for these specific capital goods players.
modes.simple: A brokerage firm has shared a list of companies in the capital goods sector they believe are good investments. This is their professional opinion on which stocks might perform well.

summary: Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL) has released its preferred stock list for the capital goods sector. Large-cap selections include ABB India, GE Vernova T&D India, and Bharat Electronics Ltd. Mid-cap picks highlighted by the brokerage are Kalpataru Projects International and Kirloskar Oil Engines. These picks reflect the brokerage's current outlook on the sector's growth potential.
why_it_matters: Brokerage sentiment may influence short-term buying interest in these stocks.
winners_losers: Listed capital goods companies gain visibility

headline: Kalpataru Projects secures Rs 2,610 crore order for South American power transmission
hook: Record international win for transmission major

modes.bear: Execution risks in overseas geographies and potential margin pressures could offset top-line growth.
modes.bull: Strong international order inflow validates global execution capabilities and expands the order book significantly.
modes.simple: Kalpataru Projects won a massive Rs 2,610 crore contract to build power lines in South America, which is good for its business growth.

summary: Kalpataru Projects International has bagged new orders worth Rs 2,610 crore, anchored by a major power transmission lines and substations project in South America. The engineering, procurement, and construction company will execute these works across international and domestic markets. Order inflows of this scale directly boost the company's executable order book and future revenue visibility. For Indian retail investors, large EPC order wins validate execution capabilities and support long-term growth prospects in the infrastructure sector.
why_it_matters: Order book expands by Rs 2,610 crore, boosting revenue visibility.

headline: Kalpataru Projects appoints Amit Uplenchwar as CEO-designate
summary: Kalpataru Projects International has named Amit Uplenchwar as Joint Managing Director and CEO-designate. He will officially take over the CEO role starting January 1, 2027. The company is currently managing a transition period to ensure leadership continuity. This appointment signals the firm's long-term succession planning for its executive management team.
whats_next: Amit Uplenchwar to assume CEO role on January 1, 2027.

headline: Kalpataru Projects reports 20.4 percent jump in Q2 net profit
hook: Strong order book backs profit growth
summary: Kalpataru Projects International posted a 20.4 percent rise in net profit to Rs 289 crore for the second quarter, up from the previous year. Revenue grew 7.3 percent to Rs 7,004 crore during the same period. The company also reported a strong order book standing at Rs 71,846 crore, supporting its execution pipeline. Retail investors tracking infrastructure stocks can evaluate order book execution trends.
why_it_matters: Robust order book supports earnings visibility for infrastructure investors.
